steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write a short introduction for a coding theory paper that constructs reduced Goppa codes from classical Goppa codes. Recall the Goppa code setup, explain the construction briefly, and state the main results on the Gilbert-Varshamov bound and decoding time.

  - designed distance \delta (lower bound for minimal distance)
  - structure polynomial g of degree \delta-1, no roots in {\rm GF}(q^{m})^{\times}; coefficients in {\rm GF}(q) for simplicity
  - notation \Gamma(g,\delta,m,q); codewords satisfy a congruence; \beta fixed primitive element of {\rm GF}(q^{m})

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Reed-Solomon codes, BCH codes, and Goppa codes are error correcting codes that are widely used, because they have fast decoding algorithms based on the Berlekamp-Massey algorithm. In this paper we construct new codes from Goppa codes. The new codes have a faster decoding algorithm, and their performance is competent to that of the classical Goppa codes.

First we recall what Goppa codes are, in a sense as narrow as possible. Like any linear code, a Goppa code has a Galois field {\rm GF}(q) as its symbol field. We require q to be a power of a small prime number, so that decoding is quick. The location field is an extension of {\rm GF}(q), say {\rm GF}(q^{m}). The set of locations is then {\mathbb{Z}}/(q^{m}-1), and this is canonically isomorphic to the multiplicative group {\rm GF}(q^{m})^{\times}. The code has a designed distance \delta, which ensures a lower bound for the minimal distance. To get a code with good performance, it has a structure polynomial g of degree \delta-1 that has no roots in {\rm GF}(q^{m})^{\times}. To keep things simple we require g to have coefficients in {\rm GF}(q). We denote the Goppa code with these parameters by \Gamma(g,\delta,m,q). Its codewords satisfy the congruence

where \beta is a fixed primitive element of {\rm GF}(q^{m}).

- Reduced Goppa codes + results
  - Fröbenius of Galois group of {\rm GF}(q^{m}) over {\rm GF}(q) acts on \Gamma(g,\delta,m,q); fixed codewords -> subcode \Gamma^{\rm F}(g,\delta,m,q)
  - delete redundance from repetition -> {\rm R}\Gamma(g,\delta,m,q), "reduced Goppa code" (Definition 2.7)
  - approach Gilbert-Varshamov bound (Theorem 4.5)
  - decoding time O(n^{2}\log^{\nu}n) in q -ary operations for codeword length n (Theorem 5.15); \nu from polynomial factorisation algorithms
  - classical Goppa codes, n=q^{m}-1: O(n^{2}\log^{\nu}n) in q^{m} -ary operations -> reduced ones decode much quicker

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Reed-Solomon codes, BCH codes, and Goppa codes are error correcting codes that are widely used, because they have fast decoding algorithms based on the Berlekamp-Massey algorithm. In this paper we construct new codes from Goppa codes. The new codes have a faster decoding algorithm, and their performance is competent to that of the classical Goppa codes.

First we recall what Goppa codes are, in a sense as narrow as possible. Like any linear code, a Goppa code has a Galois field {\rm GF}(q) as its symbol field. We require q to be a power of a small prime number, so that decoding is quick. The location field is an extension of {\rm GF}(q), say {\rm GF}(q^{m}). The set of locations is then {\mathbb{Z}}/(q^{m}-1), and this is canonically isomorphic to the multiplicative group {\rm GF}(q^{m})^{\times}. The code has a designed distance \delta, which ensures a lower bound for the minimal distance. To get a code with good performance, it has a structure polynomial g of degree \delta-1 that has no roots in {\rm GF}(q^{m})^{\times}. To keep things simple we require g to have coefficients in {\rm GF}(q). We denote the Goppa code with these parameters by \Gamma(g,\delta,m,q). Its codewords satisfy the congruence

where \beta is a fixed primitive element of {\rm GF}(q^{m}).

The Fröbenius of the Galois group of {\rm GF}(q^{m}) over {\rm GF}(q) acts on \Gamma(g,\delta,m,q), and the codewords fixed by it form a subcode \Gamma^{\rm F}(g,\delta,m,q). If we delete the redundance that comes from repetition, we get a new code {\rm R}\Gamma(g,\delta,m,q), which we call a reduced Goppa code. Definition 2.7 gives the precise construction of reduced Goppa codes. We prove that reduced Goppa codes approach to the Gilbert-Varshamov bound (see Theorem 4.5). We also prove that decoding a reduced Goppa code of codeword length n takes time O(n^{2}\log^{\nu}n) in q -ary operations (see Theorem 5.15). The constant \nu here depends on the performance of polynomial factorisation algorithms. For comparison, decoding the classical Goppa codes of codeword length n=q^{m}-1 needs O(n^{2}\log^{\nu}n) in q^{m} -ary operations. So reduced Goppa codes can be decoded much quicker than classical Goppa codes.

Acknowledgement. The author thanks Jiyou Li for pointing out some mistakes.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Reed-Solomon codes [1], BCH codes [2], [3] and Goppa codes [4] are widely used error correcting codes because of their fast decoding algorithms based on the Berlekamp-Massey algorithm [5,6]. We shall construct new codes from Goppa codes. These new codes will have a faster decoding algorithm and performances competent to the classical Goppa codes.

We recall the notion of Goppa codes in a sense as narrow as possible. As any linear code, a Goppa code has a Galois field {\rm GF}(q) as its symbol field. To ensure quick decoding, we require q to be a power of a small prime number. Its location field is an extension of {\rm GF}(q), say {\rm GF}(q^{m}), and correspondingly its set of locations is {\mathbb{Z}}/(q^{m}-1), canonically isomorphic to the multiplicative group {\rm GF}(q^{m})^{\times}. To ensure a lower bound for its minimal distance, it has a designed distance \delta. To get a code of good performance, it has a structure polynomial g of degree \delta-1 with no roots in {\rm GF}(q^{m})^{\times}. For simplicity, we require g to have coefficients in {\rm GF}(q). The Goppa code with these parameters is denoted by \Gamma(g,\delta,m,q). Its codewords satisfy the congruence

where \beta is a fixed primitive element of {\rm GF}(q^{m}).

The Fröbenius of the Galois group of {\rm GF}(q^{m}) over {\rm GF}(q) acts on \Gamma(g,\delta,m,q), and its fixed codewords form a subcode \Gamma^{\rm F}(g,\delta,m,q). Deleting the redundance caused by repetition, we obtain a new code {\rm R}\Gamma(g,\delta,m,q), which we call a reduced Goppa code. Its precise construction is given in Definition 2.7. We prove that reduced Goppa codes approach to the Gilbert-Varshamov bound (see Theorem 4.5), and that the decoding time for a reduced Goppa code of codeword length n is O(n^{2}\log^{\nu}n) in q -ary operations (see Theorem 5.15), where the constant \nu is determined by the performance of polynomial factorisation algorithms. Recall that decoding classical Goppa codes of codeword length n=q^{m}-1 requires O(n^{2}\log^{\nu}n) in q^{m} -ary operations. Hence reduced Goppa codes can be decoded much quicker than classical Goppa codes.
